tools.name: core-groups-upsert
tools.description:
Idempotent group create/update by name. Arrays replace full lists. For incremental changes use core-groups-manage instead.
📚 modyo://docs/tools/core-groups-upsert

role_id.description: Org role ID (req for create). See core-roles-manage

tools.name: core-groups-manage
tools.description:
Group lifecycle: create/update/delete/list with incremental user/site/realm changes. Org roles only (context='account'). Use core-roles-manage to find role IDs.
📚 modyo://docs/tools/core-groups-manage

groupId.description: Optional group ID for direct lookup

role_id.description: Org role ID (req for create). See core-roles-manage

verify.description: Refetch after (default: false)

tools.name: core-roles-manage
tools.description:
List roles by context. Contexts: account (groups), site (Channels), space (Content), realm (Customers). Groups require context='account'.
📚 modyo://docs/tools/core-roles-manage

tools.name: core-roles-create
tools.description:
Create a new role with optional grouped permissions.

**Params**: name (required), context (required: account/site/space/realm), grouped_permissions (optional)

**Response**: {id, key, name, context}

**Permission modules by context**:
- realm (customers): admin_originations, build_originations, view_originations_overview, view_all_submissions, edit_submissions, start_submissions, delete_submissions, assign_submissions, complete_submissions, admin_forms, admin_settings_realm
- site (channels): admin_pages, admin_templates, admin_widgets, admin_navigation, admin_settings_site
- space (content): admin_entries, admin_types, admin_categories, admin_media, admin_settings_space
- account (organization): manage_customers, manage_content, create_web_apps, admin_settings

**Note**: Use core-roles-manage to list existing roles first. Grouped permissions keys depend on context.

📚 modyo://mcp-core/tools/core-roles-create | HTTP: /docs/tools/core-roles-create

name.description: Role display name

context.description: Role context: account (organization), site (Channels), space (Content), realm (Customers)

grouped_permissions.description: Grouped permissions by module. E.g. {"customers": {"admin_originations": true, "build_originations": true}}

tools.name: core-settings-manage
tools.description:
Get or update platform settings (name, description, host, CORS, lang, cors_settings, logo, favicon, SEO, owner_id, primary_color, accent, page_background). Assets accept URLs only. Never use cors_allow_all in production.
📚 modyo://docs/tools/core-settings-manage

logo.description: Logo (URL only). null=remove. name excludes extension

name.description: Asset file name

favicon.description: Favicon (URL only). null=remove. name excludes extension

primary_hover.description: Backend primary hover color in hex

accent_hover.description: Backend accent hover color in hex

page_background.description: Backend page background color in hex

navigation_selected_text.description: Backend navigation selected text color in hex

navigation_selected_background.description: Backend navigation selected background color in hex

verify.description: Refetch after update (default: true)

tools.name: core-users-bulk
tools.description:
Bulk activate/deactivate users. Use list-affected to preview before applying. Priority: user_ids > query+filter > all. Destructive: test in staging first.
📚 modyo://docs/tools/core-users-bulk

verify.description: Count after (default: false)

tools.name: core-users-upsert
tools.description:
Idempotent user create/update by email/username. Create requires all profile fields + password (min 12). Use core-groups-manage for permissions after creation.
📚 modyo://docs/tools/core-users-upsert

tools.name: core-users-manage
tools.description:
Manage admin users: create, update, list, sessions, or get current user (me). Users start with NO permissions -- use core-groups-manage for access.
📚 modyo://docs/tools/core-users-manage

identifier.description: Email, username, or ID (req for manage/sessions)

role_id.description: Account role ID (use core-roles-manage context=account to list)

verify.description: Refetch after update (default: false)

tools.name: core-members-manage
tools.description:
Assign/update/remove users and groups to sites, spaces, and realms. Use core-roles-manage context=<contextType> for role IDs. Full names NOT reliably resolved as memberId.
📚 modyo://docs/tools/core-members-manage

tools.name: content-categories-get
tools.description: Get category details including hierarchy info. 📚 modyo://docs/tools/content-categories-get

tools.name: content-categories-list
tools.description: List categories in a space. Minimal fields by default (70% token reduction). Use content-categories-get for specific IDs. 📚 modyo://docs/tools/content-categories-list

includeDetails.description: true = full details; false = minimal fields

tools.name: content-categories-manage
tools.description: Category hierarchy management: get/create/update, delete, or list. Use parent_id for nested categories. 📚 modyo://docs/tools/content-categories-manage

identifier.description: Slug, UUID, or categoryId. Required for manage/delete.

name.description: Required for create

slug.description: Required for create; immutable after creation

parent_id.description: null = root category

verify.description: Refetch after write to confirm changes

tools.name: content-entries-get
tools.description: Get entry details including field values. Accepts ID or UUID. 📚 modyo://docs/tools/content-entries-get

entryId.description: The ID or UUID of the entry to retrieve

tools.name: content-entries-list
tools.description: List entries in a space. Returns id, uuid, name, slug, published per entry. Pass fields=['Name','Other'] (with type_id) to project field values by name in one call instead of N content-entries-get. includeDetails=true only adds administrative metadata at ~15x the tokens and never field values. 📚 modyo://docs/tools/content-entries-list

states.description: Filter by state(s): published, unpublished (includes drafts), scheduled, archived

fields.description: Field names to project into each entry, as they appear in the content type (e.g. ['Discount','Limit date']). Requires type_id. An unknown name fails the call and lists the available ones — it is never silently omitted. Assets are reduced to {name, url}. Mutually exclusive with includeDetails.

includeDetails.description: true = add administrative metadata (user.avatar, workflow config, admin url, segments_list, target_locale, dirty, status); ~90 B -> ~1.5 KB per entry. It does NOT add field values: this endpoint never returns them. Use `fields` for field values.

tools.name: content-entries-bulk

instructions:
Unified MCP Server for Modyo Platform


## Modyo MCP Server

Unified server for Modyo platform: Core, Content, Channels, Customers, Widgets. Each tool has a `📚 modyo://docs/` link — use it for detailed reference.

### Key Rules

**IDs & Stability**: Widget/Template/Entry IDs change after publishing — always use UUIDs for stable references. Bulk operations are async.
**Security**: Inline styles/scripts require `nonce="{{csp_nonce}}"`. Links must use `{{ site.url }}` prefix (never bare `/path`).
**Permissions**: Admin users start with NO access — assign to groups via `core-groups-manage`.

### Workflows
- **Content**: Create space → Define types → Create entries → Publish. Lifecycle: Draft → Published → Unpublished → Archived.
- **Channels**: Create site → Define pages → Add widgets → Publish. Widget dev: Create definition → Add code → Publish → Add to page.
- **Customers**: Create realm → Add users → Set up forms. Originations: Create → Add steps → Add questions → Publish.

### Channels — Templates & Design

**Template categories**: `layout` (page wrapper with `{{ content_for_layout }}`), `custom_snippet` (reusable via `{% snippet 'name' %}`), `system_snippet` (built-in head/header/footer — editable, NOT deletable), `stylesheet`/`javascript` (static CDN assets).

**System snippets**: ALWAYS customize `header`/`footer` via `channels-templates-upsert` with `category: "system_snippet"`. NEVER create custom_snippets for the same purpose.

**Snippet naming convention**: Use `_css` or `_js` suffix when snippet content is exclusively CSS or JavaScript (e.g. `my_widget_css`, `analytics_js`). For HTML/Liquid snippets — including system_snippets like `header`, `footer`, `head` — use no suffix.

**Layout HTML structure**: Use `{% html5 %}/{% endhtml5 %}` and `{% body %}/{% endbody %}` block tags — NEVER `{{ html5.open_tag }}`/`{{ html5.close_tag }}`. Include `{% snippet 'shared/general/body_tag_manager' %}` right after `{% body %}`.

**Snippet path derivation**: To reference a snippet via `{% snippet 'path' %}`, derive the path from the template's `path` field (from `channels-templates-find`): (1) remove the `site/` prefix, (2) remove the leading `_` and `.html.liquid` suffix from the filename. Example: `site/shared/general/_head.html.liquid` → `shared/general/head`. NEVER guess snippet paths.

**CSS token-first approach**: Read `root.css` first (Bootstrap design tokens). Override `-rgb` tokens only (`--bs-primary-rgb`, etc.). Use `base.css` for custom rules. Never use hex values directly — use `rgb(var(--bs-*-rgb))`. Prefer Bootstrap utility classes in HTML.

**CSS inclusion**: Stylesheet templates (`root.css`, `base.css`) are static CDN assets — include them in the `head` system_snippet via `{{ 'root' | asset_url: 'css' | stylesheet_tag: media: 'screen', nonce: csp_nonce }}`. NEVER use `{% stylesheet 'name' %}` in layouts — that tag does not exist in Modyo Liquid.

**New site structure**: A freshly created site already has a home page (type `home_layout_page`, path `''`) and an about page (path `'about'`), system_snippets (`head`, `header`, `footer`, etc.), and empty `root.css`/`base.css`. Customize them — do NOT recreate. New widget pages auto-use `site/base` layout; update to custom layout via `channels-pages-widget layout` param.

### Channels — Page Content Strategy

- **Widget Definitions**: Interactive components, business logic, JS, or reusable across pages. Create → publish → reference via `nameOrUuid`.
- **Content Pages**: Pages that primarily display entries from a content type (listings, indexes).
- **HTML Blocks**: Simple static content only (banners, CTAs). <30 lines; if larger, use a widget.

### Channels — Liquid Quick Reference

**Navigation**: `{% for item in menus['slug'].visible_items %}` → `item.label`, `item.url`, `item.child_items`
**Session**: `{% if user %}` (NOT `user.logged_in`). Props: `user.name`, `user.email`, `user.avatar.url`. URLs: `{{ site.url }}/login`, `{{ site.url }}/logout`.
**Search**: `<form action="{{ site.url }}/search" method="get"><input name="query"></form>`

**Links**: [Docs](https://docs.modyo.com) · [Core](https://docs.modyo.com/en/platform/core/admin/) · [Content](https://docs.modyo.com/en/platform/content/) · [Channels](https://docs.modyo.com/en/platform/channels/) · [Customers](https://docs.modyo.com/en/platform/customers/)

### Widgets

Para generar widgets transaccionales (React + Dynamic UI), el proyecto base lo inicializa el operador con `/mcp__modyo__widgets-init-project` (el Prompt `widgets-init-project` instruye invocar la Tool `widgets-scaffold`, que ejecuta el clone del template canonical al tag pineado por la compatibility matrix). Flujo de dos pasos: primero el scaffold, después el operador entrega la descripción funcional — no escribas código de widget antes de recibirla. Una vez inicializado, leé [`modyo://docs/widgets/INDEX`](modyo://docs/widgets/INDEX) para reglas críticas, patterns y workflow. Las tools `widgets-list-components`, `widgets-get-component-props`, `widgets-list-patterns` federan el catálogo del Storybook deployado de Dynamic UI; `widgets-validate` corre el validator (paquete `@modyo/widget-validator`) sobre un widget local o virtual y devuelve un `ValidationReport`. La integración opcional con Claude Code (hook `PostToolUse` para el validador) vive en [`modyo://docs/widgets/_meta-integration-claude-code`](modyo://docs/widgets/_meta-integration-claude-code).

**Catalog Resources** (read on demand, backed by versioned Storybook manifests):
- `modyo://widgets/catalog/components` — lightweight list (id, name, key, description, storyCount)
- `modyo://widgets/catalog/components/{componentId}` — full detail (stories with snippet code, props with TypeScript types, JSDoc tags)
- `modyo://widgets/catalog/patterns` — lightweight pattern list (id, name, title)
- `modyo://widgets/catalog/patterns/{patternId}` — full MDX content of a pattern story

These Resources serve official Storybook manifests from the versioned CDN. They provide richer data (story snippet code, MDX docs) than the legacy `widgets-list-*` tools. See the Pattern Discovery section below for when consultation is required.

### Pattern Discovery (REQUIRED before generating widget UI)

Before writing TSX for the widget's UI, you MUST query the catalog for an official pattern matching the domain of the request:

1. **List patterns**: read `modyo://widgets/catalog/patterns`.
2. **Identify candidates** by matching the request domain against pattern titles and ids (e.g. "transaction history" → `design-system-patterns-list-group-patterns--transaction-history`).
3. **If a candidate exists**: read `modyo://widgets/catalog/patterns/{patternId}` and use the MDX content as the structural and visual basis for the widget. Adapt to the request's specifics (data shape, locale, domain language) but PRESERVE the layout decisions, component composition, and styling conventions from the pattern.
4. **If no candidate exists**: state explicitly in the response that no official pattern matches, then proceed using only components from `modyo://widgets/catalog/components`.

Why this matters: Dynamic UI patterns embed visual decisions, density, component composition, and styling conventions that are not derivable from component props alone. Skipping this step produces widgets that are technically correct but visually generic — failing to reflect the Dynamic Framework design system.

This step is NOT optional even when the request seems simple. Patterns exist for common use cases (list views, detail panels, forms, dashboards) and apply more often than not.

### Deploy (outside the MCP)

When validation passes (widgets-validate returns passing: true), the widget is done from the MCP's perspective. Deployment runs through CI from the widget's own git repository (the scaffold initializes it with an initial commit). A manual push is the developer's explicit `modyo-cli push` in their own shell — the agent NEVER runs it.

NEVER include the user's `MODYO_TOKEN` or any credential value in the conversation. Do not read `MODYO_TOKEN` or the widget's `.env`/`.modyo` files into your own context, do not call the Modyo CLI or admin API with the token, and do not echo token material in the chat.
